bullets.title: TSMC: +10% price hike in 2027 sparks broad semi rally; SOXX +4.5%
bullets.body: TSMC is raising chip production prices 5-10% for advanced and mature nodes starting Jan 2027, with up to 15% premium for high-volume HPC orders; price negotiations concluded in July. The announcement sparked a broad semiconductor rally with SOXX up ~4.5% premarket, memory names surging (Kioxia +17%, Samsung +6%), and most semis up 4-6% (MU +6.3%, MRVL +5.7%, INTC +5.9%, ARM +5.1%). TSMC also raised 2026 capex guidance to $60-64B from $52-56B, citing tool inflation, and reiterated 40%+ YoY revenue growth for 2026.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley software sweep: ADBE to UW/$240, CRM/INTU/WDAY downgraded; MSFT OW/$600
bullets.body: MS analyst Adam Wood assumed coverage of the software sector, downgrading ADBE to Underweight from Equal-Weight (PT $240 from $365) citing multi-transition execution risk, CRM and INTU to Equal-Weight (PTs $185 and $335 from $287 and $580), and WDAY to Underweight ($145 from $185). MSFT assumed Overweight at $600 (cut from $650) on Azure >40% YoY growth and Copilot monetization. High-conviction OW names include PANW raised to Top Pick at $387, CRWD to $227, and U upgraded to OW at $35. NOW, SHOP, TEAM assumed Overweight at $180, $192, $120 respectively.

bullets.title: NVDA raises NBIS stake to 9.3%; NBIS +6.8% premarket
bullets.body: Nvidia filed a 13G disclosing its passive stake in Nebius Group increased to 9.3% (22.26M shares including ~21M from a $2B prefunded warrant) from 0.55% as of March 31. NBIS surged ~6.8% premarket on the disclosure.

bullets.title: META: Jefferies upgrades to Buy/$825 on $14-18B AI glasses opportunity
bullets.body: Jefferies initiated a BUY on META at $825 PT (vs. $646, +28% upside) based on a $14-18B hardware revenue opportunity from AI glasses at Apple Watch-scale adoption (~35-45M units at $400 ASP). Meta AI MAUs reached ~1B and daily glasses users are tripling YoY with 7M+ units sold in 2025; EssilorLuxottica doubling production to 20M units in 2026. JPM also reported META is in talks to lease AI compute to Anthropic for ~$10B over two years, and BlackRock is leading a $12B debt financing for Meta data centers in Texas.

bullets.title: ORCL: 50%+ decline since June; $7B Wisconsin collateral risk; Mizuho upgrades to Outperform
bullets.body: Oracle has collapsed >50% since June, with default risk protection at multi-year highs on AI debt load concerns and potential $7B+ collateral requirement for its Wisconsin data center under stricter power-regulator credit rules. Despite this, Mizuho upgraded ORCL to Outperform, noting shares trade at 14x CY27 EPS (multi-year low), 1GW capacity coming in F1Q27, $8B+ contracts with key customers, and $40B in new fundraising to fund expansion; models FCF turning positive at $8B in FY29.

bullets.title: GOOGL/TSLA: Big Tech earnings kick off Wed; Street focused on cloud, AI capex, robotaxi
bullets.body: Alphabet (reporting Wednesday after market, $2.88 EPS / $117B revenue consensus) faces scrutiny on cloud growth, Gemini 3.5 Pro delay rationale, and Frozen v2 chip—a custom ASIC expected in 2028 with 6-10x efficiency over current TPUs. KeyBanc maintains $445 PT. Tesla reports Wednesday; focus on robotaxi unsupervised ramp timeline (245 Cybercabs at Giga Texas visible but deemed unscalable without unsupervised autonomy), Optimus production, and margin trajectory. Hedgeye issued a 'Do NOT Buy' call into TSLA earnings.

bullets.title: AMD: Helios AI platform launches with MI455X + EPYC; Microsoft Azure adoption confirmed
bullets.body: AMD unveiled Helios, a next-gen AI platform with MI455X GPUs and 6th Gen EPYC, beginning Azure customer shipments in H2 2026. Microsoft deploying AMD Helios reinforces supply diversity and cost-per-token themes vs NVDA. Citi notes AMD MI450 carries 432GB HBM4 vs NVDA Vera Rubin's 288GB; AMD data center share could rise from 4.5% to 20-25% per Futurum Group. Citi also flagged AMD Instinct secured OpenAI, Meta, Oracle (50k units) contracts. SMH IV at 98th percentile ahead of AMD conference.

bullets.title: MU: BofA adds to US 1 List; DRAM prices surging in early July
bullets.body: Bank of America added Micron to its US 1 List of top stock picks. South Korean DRAM unit prices are accelerating sharply in July 1-20 data with upward momentum intensifying, supporting the bull case for MU and the broader memory complex.

bullets.title: INTC: Fresh data center layoffs; Xeon 6 memory bandwidth BIOS update
bullets.body: Intel is planning a new round of layoffs targeting its Data Center and AI Group despite 22% 1Q26 revenue growth, as part of a broader strategy to become more focused and efficient. On the positive side, Intel released a BIOS update for select Xeon 6 SKUs enabling 8000 MT/s memory bandwidth.

bullets.title: SNAP: Settlement reached in social media addiction litigation; META faces trial next week
bullets.body: Snap is nearing settlement in social media addiction litigation while Meta remains the only defendant facing trial in Los Angeles next week, according to JPM's morning note.

bullets.title: LYV: Susquehanna downgrades to Neutral, PT raised to $186; JPM bullish at $205
bullets.body: Susquehanna downgraded Live Nation to Neutral from Positive but raised the PT to $186 from $181 (3% upside vs. $180.86 current). JPM remains more bullish with a $205 PT, citing double-digit ticket sales growth and stadium/amphitheater weighted to 2H 2026.

bullets.title: NOW/HUBS: NOW earnings Wed; Piper constructive on AI pricing uplift; HUBS channel checks muted
bullets.body: ServiceNow (reporting Wednesday) is highlighted as constructive by Piper Sandler on solid demand and AI pricing (Prime/Advanced/Foundation) with 20-30% uplift and margin upside. UBS's HUBS channel checks show more muted tone: AI adoption building but early monetization (~$30-35M FY26 AI credit revenue, ~1pt growth contribution); UBS maintains Buy at $250 PT.

bullets.title: SHOP: Mixed signals—Morgan Stanley OW/$192 vs. Rothschild downgrade to Neutral/$130
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley assumed SHOP Overweight at $192 PT (54% upside), viewing it as a later-cycle AI beneficiary in commerce. Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded SHOP to Neutral from Buy, cutting PT to $130 from $160, citing Meta competition as a key headwind. The morning pre-market note also showed SHOP -4.7% on MS's broader software coverage reset.

bullets.title: DDOG: Jefferies downgrades to Hold; PT raised to $280 from $210 on valuation
bullets.body: Jefferies analyst Brent Thill downgraded Datadog to Hold from Buy, citing valuation after the stock's run; the PT was raised to $280 from $210, implying only 6% upside vs. $263.

bullets.title: GLW: Morgan Stanley maintains EW/$180; Q2 modest upside, key focus on 3Q optical ramp
bullets.body: GLW fell ~40% from its late-June GlassBridge peak. MS sees Q2 revenue upside limited (~$50M), with the key debate being whether Street's ~$200M sequential Q3 optical revenue growth estimate is achievable. GLW positioned as architecture-agnostic across CPO/NPO/LPO; management targets 2028 for meaningful optical scale-up adoption. Bear/base/bull case PT: $72/$180/$230.

bullets.title: FWONK/TKO/SPHR: Live entertainment 'funflation' intact; FWONK preferred at 22x vs. TKO 30x
bullets.body: JPM previews live entertainment Q2: LYV/FWONK top picks. FWONK 2026 EBITDA ~$1B; Formula 1 team payments imply ~$1.35B annualized with Turkey and new races in 2027 as catalysts; valued at 22x '27 LFCF vs. TKO at 30x. TKO Q2 EBITDA revised down to $638M on White House event costs but full-year $2.27B guidance intact. SPHR WoZ contributed ~$123M to Q2 revenue.

bullets.title: VZ/T/CMCSA/CHTR: Cable broadband losses deepen; wireless pricing firm; earnings this week
bullets.body: JPM previews Big-3 wireless: EBITDA beats expected with healthy pricing (AT&T raised admin fee, T-Mobile migrating 8M legacy customers up to $6/line). Cable broadband net losses forecast at 555k in 2Q26 (vs. 480k prior year) as Starlink scales toward 12.19M US subs by 2030. CMCSA reports Thursday (EPS $0.97, revenue $29.24B), CHTR Friday ($9.98, $13.51B), VZ Friday ($1.28, $35.16B).

bullets.title: SNDK: Evercore $3,100 PT; memory cycle in focus as NAND shortage to ease in 2027
bullets.body: Evercore issued a $3,100 PT on SanDisk (SNDK), implying >100% upside. TrendForce projects NAND supply shortage to ease in 2027 as servers account for >40% of NAND bit demand. Samsung separately ramping V-NAND supply to NVIDIA for its Context Memory Storage launching 2H.

bullets.title: AAPL: Trading at 11x sales, highest valuation in history; Apple AI China launch as catalyst
bullets.body: Apple is trading at nearly 11x sales, the highest valuation in company history (10-year median ~6.6x). Morgan Stanley is positioning Apple AI launch in China as a key catalyst, highlighted in its ASML roadshow webcast. Oppenheimer's sector top-pick list includes AAPL as a Buy.

bullets.title: IONQ: Jefferies Buy/$85 PT on quantum computing momentum; government program backing
bullets.body: Jefferies strategist Chris Wood maintains IonQ at Buy with an $85 PT, noting quantum computing gained traction from Trump's June executive orders backed by ~$2B federal program and a 20x oversubscribed Quantinuum IPO.
